chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them), who said:
The Angel does not write down except what he hears,
and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, Says: 'And remember your Lord within yourself humbly and fearing.'
So no one knows the reward of that remembrance in the self of the man apart from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, due to His greatness.

key_terms.الْمَلَكُ: The Angel (specifically the recorder of deeds)

ai.seo_question: Why is private remembrance of God (Dhikr) considered more profound in terms of reward?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the spiritual intimacy of private dhikr, noting that angels record only what is perceptible, whereas Allah’s omniscience encompasses the hidden sincerity of the heart. It underscores the Shia emphasis on the inner dimension of worship, where the reward is directly tied to God’s awareness of the believer’s internal state rather than external observation. This aligns with the concept of 'ikhlas' (sincerity), where the act is performed solely for God, unseen by creation.
